newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen steel unit profit down, but sees upturn.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen steel unit profit down, but sees upturn.

text.p: Thyssen Stahl AG, Germany's largest steel maker, said on Thursday its 1995-96 profits dropped sharply, but Chief Executive Ekkehard Schulz said a cyclical trough was over and the outlook has improved.
Group net profit at the steel unit of Thyssen AG fell to 174 million German marks ($109 million) in the year ended Sept. 30 from a record 651 million marks ($407 million) the year before.
Sales fell to 10.6 billion marks ($6.6 billion) from 11.9 billion marks ($7.4 billion).
A cyclical fall in steel demand, with a consequent 10 percent decline in steel prices, was the main reason for the weak results, Schulz told reporters.

Sales in the first quarter of 1996-97 were 2.1 billion marks ($1.3 billion), down 19 percent even after accounting for divisions that were spun off last October. Crude steel production in the quarter was up 11 percent, however.

Schulz, speaking against a backdrop of smoke-belching furnaces, said the steel business was back on an uptrend. He said he shared the view of the German steel association that national crude steel output would rise 5 percent to nearly 42 million metric tons in 1997.
